experiments.paper_location: Section 4.3.2 Vectorizing Sparse-Dense and Dense-Sparse Operations
experiments.mechanism: Compute dense OI forward dot products with AVX-512 while preserving bias and handling vector tails.

conditions.oracle: scalar FP32 dot product plus non-zero bias

experiments.note: The focused kernel oracle covers the arithmetic contract and boundary sizes; the maintained full Layer path is separately exercised by the AVX smoke workflow.

experiments.mechanism: Union candidates from L queried buckets, guarantee softmax labels are present, and fill a small candidate set from the layer random-node order.

conditions.oracle: fixed bucket contents, labels, random-node order, and fill start

experiments.note: The helper preserves the maintained Mode=4 policy while separating deterministic candidate semantics from hash computation and the time-seeded choice of fill start.

experiments.paper_location: Section 4.3.2 Vectorizing Sparse-Dense and Dense-Sparse Operations
experiments.mechanism: Vectorize OI backward gradients in complete 128-input blocks and use the scalar path when an input tail is present.

conditions.oracle: scalar weight/input gradient formulas for a complete 128-input block

experiments.note: The historical unrolled path dropped non-128 input tails. The maintained port now selects that path only for complete 128-input blocks.

experiments.paper_location: Section 3.1; Algorithm 1 sparse feed-forward and backpropagation
experiments.mechanism: Compute an active neuron's affine/ReLU value from sparse input indices and accumulate first-layer gradients only for those active input coordinates.

conditions.oracle: explicit w*x+b and delta*x formulas
conditions.optimizer: ADAM gradient accumulator before optimizer step

experiments.note: Separates sparse arithmetic from LSH candidate selection. The test covers gradient accumulation, not Network::ProcessInput's later full-array Adam state update.

experiments.paper_location: Section 4.1 Memory Layout Optimizations; Section 4.3 vectorized computation
experiments.mechanism: Represent the same weight matrix in output-input (OI) or input-output (IO) order without changing sparse forward or gradient semantics.

conditions.oracle: same logical dense matrix encoded in both layouts

experiments.note: Arithmetic/layout oracle independent of AVX hardware; full maintained Layer paths remain covered by scalar and AVX smoke jobs.

experiments.mechanism: Run the maintained Layer Mode 4 query path through LSH lookup, deterministic candidate helper wiring, filler semantics, and sparse activation evaluation.

conditions.oracle: all nodes are filled because node_count < target; ReLU values match explicit sparse w*x+b

experiments.note: This runtime integration fixture verifies that Layer uses the extracted sampling helper without replacing the historical time-seeded fill start. Because the fixture has four nodes, the final active set is deterministic regardless of the selected start offset.

experiments.paper_location: Section 2 LSH background and the hash-family choices used by the released SLIDE implementation
experiments.mechanism: Select winner positions inside WTA/DWTA bins, preserve deterministic tie behavior, densify empty bins from valid probes, and keep hash components in the bin-value domain consumed by (K,L) packing.

conditions.tie_rule: first maximum wins because replacement uses strict greater-than
conditions.dwta_empty_bin: resolved from a fixed probe sequence

experiments.note: WTA/DWTA are prerequisite LSH families used by the released implementation. This test does not treat their standalone algorithmic details as a new SLIDE paper contribution.

experiments.mechanism: Normalize selected output activations with Softmax and form target-minus-probability deltas on the selected class set.

conditions.oracle: explicit exp(logit-max)/sum and target-minus-probability

experiments.note: The implementation stores the sign convention used by the released update path; the test validates that convention rather than relabeling it as a generic loss-gradient sign.

experiments.mechanism: Propagate an output delta through only the active previous-layer nodes, respecting the previous ReLU gate while accumulating selected weight and bias gradients.

conditions.oracle: delta*w through positive ReLU activation and delta*a for selected weights

experiments.note: Separates active-path backpropagation from the later layer-wide optimizer traversal.

experiments.paper_location: Optimizer prerequisite used by the released training implementation
experiments.mechanism: Update Adam first/second moments and a parameter using the current gradient and historical optimizer state.

conditions.oracle: explicit Adam moment/velocity/parameter formula

experiments.note: Shows that a currently zero sparse gradient can still move a parameter through historical momentum; sparse gradient accumulation is not equivalent to sparse optimizer-state traversal.

experiments.mechanism: Decide fixed record-count rehash/rebuild boundaries independently and make rebuild imply an effective table rehash for sparse layers.
experiments.note: The maintained driver uses fixed intervals. The paper additionally describes increasing the interval over training, so this schedule is tracked as an implementation variant rather than a literal reproduction of that heuristic.

experiments.mechanism: Clear and repopulate the LSH table after parameter updates, optionally regenerating the hash function first, while keeping each Node's stored table/bucket positions consistent.

conditions.rebuild: generation increments and table is repopulated

experiments.note: The integration fixture checks state consistency after both transitions; rebuild always includes rehash in the maintained port.

experiments.mechanism: Exercise real optimized Layer objects in OI and IO physical layouts with the same logical weights, sparse inputs, forward activations, and backward gradients.

conditions.oracle: explicit logical W*x+b, dW=dy*x, db=dy, dx=dy*W with ReLU gate

experiments.note: This closes the gap between layout-only arithmetic oracles and the maintained Layer implementation; AVX-specific arithmetic remains covered separately by hardware-gated tests.

experiments.mechanism: Distinguish mode 1 FP32 weight storage from mode 2 BF16 compute-word plus low-word FP32 master storage, and apply scalar Adam in FP32 master precision.

conditions.mode2: BF16 activations/compute weights with split high+low FP32 optimizer state
conditions.oracle: bit-exact split round trip; real Layer forward semantics; explicit scalar Adam formula

experiments.note: Mode 2 compute uses the BF16 high word, while scalar optimizer updates reconstruct and rewrite the full FP32 master value. This test also protects against treating bfloat16-to-uint16 conversion as raw-bit extraction.

experiments.mechanism: Use native AVX-512 BF16 conversion and dot-product instructions and compare their result with an explicit scalar BF16-RNE reference.

conditions.oracle: scalar RNE conversion of 32 FP32 operands followed by BF16-rounded dot product
conditions.execution: hardware-gated; CPU information emitted before execution

experiments.note: The test is skipped only when the GitHub-hosted runner does not expose AVX-512 BF16.

conditions.gate_true: example mining enabled and triplet loss evaluated once

experiments.mechanism: Construct positive examples from the largest post-mask/post-softmax attention probability and negative examples from the raw pre-mask dot-product argmin used by the released Reformer path.

conditions.oracle: fixed candidate-index tensor, attention probabilities, and negative argmin positions

experiments.note: This records the released example-mining rule around the paper's positive/negative training concept; it is not presented as a verbatim statement of Equation 3.

experiments.paper_location: Section 3.3 learnable LSH; released SLIDE-side implementation variant

conditions.oracle: explicit tanh agreement followed by sigmoid BCE

experiments.note: This objective is separate from the Reformer-side cosine-margin triplet objective and is not a literal implementation of Equation 3.
